Let $a:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative complex dimension $d$. Smooth analytic local charts identify it, locally on source and target, with $\operatorname{pr}:W\times V\to V$, where $W$ is an oriented complex $d$-ball; $V$ need not be smooth. For an open $V'\subseteq V$, the generator $E_{W\times V'}=j_{W\times V'!}k$ has proper-support image $E_{V'}\otimes_kR\Gamma_c(W,k)=E_{V'}[-2d]$, by the finite oriented ball relative-cochain model of [F2] and the support construction of [F1]. For any bounded constructible $B$ on $V$, the ordinary product comparison of [F2] gives $R\Gamma(W\times V',\operatorname{pr}^*B)=R\Gamma(V',B)$ because $W$ is contractible. Consequently $R\operatorname{Hom}(E_{W\times V'},\operatorname{pr}^*B[2d])=R\operatorname{Hom}(R\operatorname{pr}_!E_{W\times V'},B)$. The orientation integration map $R\operatorname{pr}_!\operatorname{pr}^*B[2d]\to B$ transposes under [F3] to a comparison $\operatorname{pr}^*B[2d]\to\operatorname{pr}^!B$, and on these generators its Hom map is exactly the displayed cochain evaluation isomorphism, natural under shrinking product charts; the exceptional adjoint of [F3] identifies the same right-hand complex with $R\operatorname{Hom}(E_{W\times V'},\operatorname{pr}^!B)$. Product opens form a neighbourhood basis, so the comparisons identify derived sections and hence cohomology stalks, proving $\operatorname{pr}^!B\simeq\operatorname{pr}^*B[2d]$. The positive complex orientation makes the local comparisons agree on overlaps, so they glue to $a^!\simeq a^*[2d]$ on all bounded constructible inputs. The orientation generator maps to $1\in k$ over every field, including characteristic two. This proves the relative formula on arbitrary constructible complexes rather than only on smooth local systems. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4]

Since $D$ is a subcomplex, a simplex of $K$ is contained in $D$ as soon as one of its faces is, so the set $P$ of simplices outside $D$ is closed under taking faces; hence $q^{-1}(P_{\ge\sigma})=\{x\in X:\sigma\subseteq q(x)\}=\operatorname{St}(\sigma)$, because a point of $|K|$ whose carrier contains $\sigma$ cannot lie in $|D|$ and every face of a simplex of $P$ again lies in $P$. The star $\operatorname{St}(\sigma)=\bigcup_{\tau\supseteq\sigma}\tau^\circ$ is open in $|K|$, since its trace on each closed simplex $|\eta|$ is $\{x\in|\eta|:\sigma\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(x)\}$, which is relatively open when $\sigma\subseteq\eta$ and empty otherwise; being contained in $X$ it is also open in $X$. As the principal upsets form a basis, $q$ is continuous. Each $\sigma^\circ$ is convex in the affine simplex spanned by $\sigma$, hence connected, locally path-connected and simply connected, and each $\operatorname{St}(\sigma)$ is open and nonempty. Now let $\sigma\in P$. If $\sigma\not\subseteq\tau$ then $\operatorname{St}(\sigma)\cap|\tau|=\varnothing$ and the cohomology vanishes. If $\sigma\subseteq\tau$, then in barycentric coordinates on $\tau$ the set $\operatorname{St}(\sigma)\cap|\tau|=\{x\in|\tau|:\sigma\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(x)\}$ is described by strict inequalities $\lambda_v>0$ for $v\in\sigma$, non-strict inequalities $\lambda_v\ge0$ for the remaining vertices, and $\sum_v\lambda_v=1$; it is convex, nonempty, and contracts by the straight-line homotopy to its barycentre, and it is a metric space with a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets, being an intersection of convex sets with small euclidean balls. So [F7] gives $H^0=W$ and $H^q=0$ for $q>0$. Realized standard injectives are therefore acyclic for the functors $\Gamma(\operatorname{St}(\sigma),-)$ and $\Gamma(X,-)$, and so are their finite direct sums, since cohomology is additive in finite direct sums. Hence [F8] identifies its cohomology on open $V\subseteq X$ with the constant cohomology of $V\cap Z_\tau$. If $\sigma\not\subseteq\tau$ the star intersection is empty. Otherwise $\operatorname{St}(\sigma)\cap Z_\tau=\operatorname{St}(\sigma)\cap|\tau|$, since any point in that star has a coface of the retained $\sigma$ and cannot lie in $D$. The intersection is convex and contractible in barycentric coordinates, with constant-sheaf cohomology $W$ in degree zero and zero above by [F7]. These computations show the realized standard injectives, and their finite sums, are acyclic for ordinary global sections and for each retained star. No deleted face is included in $X$. edits.after: 3.1 Constant coefficients and sharpness for hard truncation. For $F=k_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$, so the actual total-degree computation uses the outgoing map from level $n$ to level $n+1$. To see that omitting that map can change the answer in every degree, take the proper surjection from two reduced points $S=\{0,1\}$ to a point and its Cech nerve. The normalized degree-$p$ cochains are $k^2$, indexed by the two alternating nondegenerate strings of length $p+1$. Interior deletions give degenerate strings and vanish in the normalized differential; the two endpoint deletions give $\delta_p(v_0,v_1)=(v_1+(-1)^{p+1}v_0,v_0+(-1)^{p+1}v_1)$, which has rank one over every field. The full augmented complex is contracted by inserting one point, as in [F1], so its positive cohomology is zero and $H^0=k$. If one retains only cochain levels $0,\ldots,n$ and discards $\delta_n$, its top cohomology is $k$ for $n>0$ and $k^2$ for $n=0$, giving the wrong answer. Thus level $n+1$ is necessary in general for this hard truncation of the cochain data. A coskeleton truncation is different: it reconstructs higher levels from matching limits, so no claim that $\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_nX_\bullet$ itself fails descent is made. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

4.3 **Connected fibres and local systems.** Each $\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ is path connected: Gaussian elimination expresses an invertible matrix as a product of elementary matrices and nonzero diagonal matrices, each joined to the identity by a path. Each frame space $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i})$ is the continuous image of connected $\operatorname{GL}_{N_i}(\mathbb C)$ under its first-$n_i$-columns map, so $U_N$ is connected. A locally trivial bundle with connected fibre induces a surjection on fundamental groups: lift a base loop locally and join its endpoint to its initial point inside the fibre. Thus on a connected smooth invariant stratum $S$ both $q_N:U_N\times S\to S_N$ and $\operatorname{pr}_S:U_N\times S\to S$ induce surjective fundamental-group maps. Local trivializations define parallel transport by subdivision along paths; subdivision of a homotopy square proves homotopy invariance, and a sub-local-system is exactly a subspace of one stalk invariant under this loop transport, extended to all stalks by transport. Thus these pullbacks preserve and reflect irreducibility, since the full monodromy image is unchanged. If $L$ is an equivariant local system and $L_N=Q_NL$, any ordinary sub-local-system $M_N\subset L_N$ pulls back to a sub-local-system of $\operatorname{pr}_S^*L$. On the product the $U_N$ factor acts trivially on this monodromy representation and its subrepresentations, so $q_N^*M_N=\operatorname{pr}_S^*M$ for a local system $M$ on $S$. The actual resolution-image criterion in ordinary interval $[0,0]$ descends $M_N$ to an equivariant local system and the degree-zero Hom comparison lifts its injection. Hence $L$ is simple equivariantly if and only if $L_N$ is irreducible ordinarily, and by the connected-fibre pullbacks if and only if its underlying local system on $S$ is irreducible. [F3, F4, given]

4.4 **Underlying ordinary simplicity.** The equivariant truncations of step 4.1 and the localization adjunctions of [F4] define intermediate extension by the image of ${}^pH^0j_!\to{}^pH^0Rj_*$. A simple equivariant heart object $A$ has irreducible invariant support $Z$: the finite support components are permuted by connected $G$, hence individually invariant, and localization on a dense component would otherwise yield a nonzero proper subobject. Choose the invariant dense smooth open where its ordinary cohomology is locally constant; equivariance preserves this locus and algebraic constructibility gives a dense algebraic such open. The perverse inequalities force restriction there to be a local system $L[\dim Z]$. A proper equivariant sub-local-system yields a proper subobject by localization adjunction and perverse image, so $L$ is simple equivariantly. Absence of boundary subobjects and quotients identifies $A$ with $j_{!*}L[\dim Z]$ by the image and adjunction characterization of [F2]. Restriction is perverse exact by step 2.1 and commutes with localization in [F4], hence with that image. Step 4.3 makes $L$ irreducible ordinarily, so $A_X$ is the ordinary simple intersection complex of [F2]. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 4.3]

4.5 **Preservation after normalization.** Smooth dimension-shifted pullback along a locally trivial map with connected smooth fibres preserves ordinary simple intersection complexes: the fundamental-group surjection preserves irreducibility on the dense smooth open, smooth local product comparison commutes with $j_!$ and $Rj_*$ on boundary charts, and perverse exactness carries their intermediate-extension image to the same image upstairs. Here the fibres are irreducible frame spaces, so the inverse image of an irreducible support is irreducible. Apply this to $\operatorname{pr}_X$, with fibre $U_N$. For simple equivariant $A$, step 4.4 makes $A_X$ simple, so $\operatorname{pr}_X^*A_X[u_N]$ is simple. By step 1.1 this is $q_N^*(Q_N(A)[s_N])[g]$. Any nonzero proper subobject of $Q_N(A)[s_N]$ would give one upstairs through exact conservative $q_N^*[g]$, a contradiction. Thus normalization preserves simplicity; reflection is step 4.2 and concentration is step 2.1. Both directions use the same $s_N=u_N-g$ and stated ring-comparison threshold, with the actual product of connected general linear groups. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.2, step 4.4]
